proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the adjacent-root reroot identity, operator-valued Shapley defect, exact invariance criterion, sharp attainable root-indexed set, and an exact O(n^3 q^2) rational algorithm for positive finite-alphabet tree laws. Both final correctness panels passed after repairing the binary zero-row-sum argument, but the cold paper-level review capped the package at incremental; reaching the field floor would require finite-sample inference, a substantive decision application, or a broader graph class, each a separate research program.
tldr: For strictly positive rational finite-alphabet tree laws and a rational target score, observable edge transitions give an exact criterion for when old/new mechanism-change Shapley vectors agree across every collider-free root. They also give the sharp root-indexed vector set, categorical SCM witnesses, and an exact matrix-message algorithm. The binary target-mean formulas are the two-state identity-score specialization. A faithful binary two-node example establishes observational nonidentifiability in the broader supplied-DAG Budhathoki class.
gap: Budhathoki et al. explicitly raise graph uncertainty for their mechanism-change Shapley game. Verified MEC prediction-explanation, do-intervention class-enumeration, graph-agnostic intervention-localization, ordered metric-attribution, and fixed-order change-inference results address different games, targets, graph classes, or observation regimes. On a rooted tree Witter et al.’s irreducible do-game classes are already polynomially many, but their class values do not determine old/new mechanism-swap values. No inspected statement supplies the positive binary-tree mean-game reroot criterion or exact root-indexed set.
